together to celebrate the Eucharist which in Greek eucharisteo means to give thanks th This weekend November 21 22 the Church celebrates the Solemnity of Jesus Christ King of the Universe Pope Pius XI originally created this solemnity as a feast day in 1925 Following the horrific loss of life experienced during the Great War Pius saw how the world was drifting away from Jesus Christ and hoped that this feast day would help reawaken societys recognition of Jesus st nd Perhaps prophetically Pius cautioned that as individuals and states refuse to submit to the rule of our Savior there will be no really hopeful prospect of a lasting peace among nations Instead when societies reject Christ they collapse and war too often follows It is only when we recognize both in private and in public life that Christ is King society will at last receive the great blessings of real liberty wellordered discipline peace harmony Next weekend we celebrate the start of a new liturgical year with the First Sunday of Advent This new year will continue our threeyear lectionary cycle as we enter into Year and the Gospel of St Mark with a brief interlude from the Gospel of St John and the Bread of Life Discourse in the middle of Ordinary Time This structure places the Eucharist at the very center of our lectionary cycle The Gospel of St Mark was written by St Mark also known as John Mark a traveling companion mentioned throughout the New Testament in connection with Sts Peter Paul and Barnabas Mark stresses Jesus messages about the kingdom of God now breaking into human life as good news and how Jesus himself is the gospel or good news of God Jesus is Himself the very Son whom God sent into the world to rescue humanity by serving others and by sacrificing His life for us Traditionally the gospel is said to have been written shortly before AD 70 in Rome amid impending persecution and as destruction loomed over Jerusalem Its audience seems to have been Gentile unfamiliar with Jewish customs The Gospel aimed to equip such Christians to stand faithful in the face of persecution while still continuing to proclaim the gospel to others ADVENT MISSION AND FORTY HOURS DEVOTION Though Advent is still a week away we are announcing a SAVE THE DATE for our upcoming Advent Parish Mission and Forty Hours Devotion This year we are combining these two important events to support our spiritual preparation for Christmas On the Second Sunday of Advent we welcome Fr Ben Cameron of the Fathers of Mercy as the homilist at all of our weekend Masses Fr Cameron will preach in preparation for our Parish Mission Then on Sunday evening Dec 6 at 7:00PM Fr Cameron will offer the first of four mission talks The four talks will be at 7:00PM each evening Sunday through Wednesday Dec 9th th On Monday Dec 7 Fr Camerons second talk will be offered as the homily for our 7:00PM Vigil Mass for the Holy Day of the Immaculate Conception At the end of this Mass we will begin our annual Forty Hours Devotion with the start of Adoration Adoration will continue nonstop except during Mass times from Monday evening to the end of the parish mission on Wednesday evening th One way we express our devotion to the reign of Christ the King is by freely giving Him our time I would strongly encourage each of us to sign up for an hour of adoration throughout the Forty Hours If you have never had the opportunity to spend time in adoration now is the time You will be amazed at how the Lord will speak to you in the quiet of your heart if you but make this time for Him Liturgical Ministers Schedule
